the distribution of psychiatric cases in the Medicare population is not uniform, that the distribution is affected by changes in the Medicare payment system, that the distribution differs from one state to another, and that it is difficult to determine whether the distribution reflects the distribution of cases in the Medicare beneficiary population or the distribution of cases within the Medicare population.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we should be very careful when we use the term ‘mental health’ because it is not a monolith and there are different types of mental health problems that require different types of interventions.
the Medicare program is not a good indicator of the overall mental health care system, as it only represents a small portion of the population.
